## Data Breach Response  
**If You Discover a Breach:**
1. Stop further access
2. Report to manager immediately
3. Report to DPO (dpo@firstuk.bank)
4. Do NOT attempt to cover it up
5. DPO will notify FCA and customers within 72 hours  
**Consequences of Breach:**
- Customer notification required
- FCA notification required
- Reputational damage
- Potential fines (up to €20M or 4% revenue)
- Criminal prosecution possible

raw_entities.name: Data Breach Reporting Obligation
raw_entities.description: Staff must immediately report any discovered data breach to their manager and the Data Protection Officer. The DPO is responsible for notifying the FCA and affected customers within 72 hours of discovery. Attempting to cover up a breach is explicitly prohibited.
context: Do NOT attempt to cover it up
DPO will notify FCA and customers within 72 hours

raw_entities.name: Data Breach Non-Concealment Obligation
raw_entities.description: Staff are explicitly prohibited from attempting to conceal or cover up any data breach. This is a mandatory transparency requirement tied to regulatory and criminal consequences.
context: Do NOT attempt to cover it up

raw_entities.name: Data Breach Access Containment Obligation
raw_entities.description: Upon discovery of a data breach, staff must immediately stop any further unauthorized access to the affected data or systems.

raw_entities.name: Data Breach Discovery
raw_entities.description: The identification or discovery of unauthorized access to customer data or systems constitutes a critical warning sign requiring immediate escalation and containment action.

raw_entities.name: Data Protection Officer
raw_entities.description: The designated Data Protection Officer responsible for receiving breach reports from staff and managing regulatory notifications to the FCA and affected customers within the required 72-hour timeframe.
context: DPO will notify FCA and customers within 72 hours
